summary: The bill nullifies the March 27, 2025 executive order that excludes certain federal employees from labor-management relations programs, bars use of federal funds to implement it, and keeps all collective bargaining agreements in effect as of March 26, 2025, fully valid through their stated terms.

scores.thoughts: The bill explicitly prohibits obligating or expending federal funds to implement the nullified Executive Order. This is a narrow, one-time restriction on spending tied to a specific administrative action rather than a broad fiscal policy change, so the effect on overall government spending is minimal and tangential.
The bill contains no provisions related to tax rates, tax policy, revenue collection, or any tax-related matters.
The bill addresses federal labor-management relations and collective bargaining agreements; it has no connection to healthcare policy, coverage, or markets.
No provisions in the bill relate to firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
The legislation deals solely with federal employee labor relations and does not address immigration, border policy, or pathways to citizenship.
The bill makes no reference to reproductive rights, abortion access, or related regulations.
While the bill applies government-wide to executive branch agencies (which could include defense civilians), it does not alter military budgets, force structure, or defense spending levels.
No environmental, regulatory, or climate-related provisions appear in the text.
The bill does not modify any welfare, entitlement, or social safety-net programs.
No education policy, school funding, or school-choice provisions are present.
The legislation contains nothing related to drug enforcement, decriminalization, or substance regulation.
No provisions address sentencing, policing, incarceration, or criminal justice reform.
The bill does not touch on tariffs, trade agreements, or globalization issues.
The single clause limiting funds for the Executive Order has negligible impact on deficit or debt trajectory; the bill is not a fiscal policy measure.
No language addresses LGBTQ protections, anti-discrimination rules, or related civil rights.
The bill makes no changes to foreign assistance programs or funding.
Nothing in the bill pertains to voting access, election administration, or voter ID requirements.
The legislation does not regulate technology companies, data privacy, or digital oversight.

The core purpose of the bill is to nullify an Executive Order that excluded agencies from federal labor-management relations programs and to preserve existing collective bargaining agreements. This directly strengthens union rights and collective bargaining for federal employees, aligning strongly with the worker-protection end of the spectrum.
No provisions address religious exemptions, civil rights enforcement, or conflicts between religious liberty and anti-discrimination rules.
